title: Why MCP Threw Away Sessions in 2026
description:
Stateless MCP explained in 60 seconds: the Model Context Protocol specification 2026-07-28 removed the initialize handshake and the session ID (Mcp-Session-Id).
Now every MCP request carries what it needs, so any MCP server can answer it. Told with a diner: one waiter with your order in his head, or an order slip any waiter can take.

Status: shipped. 2026-07-28 is the current MCP protocol version (released July 28, 2026). Before it, revision 2025-11-25 started with a handshake and could pin you to one server with a session ID.

Chapters
0:00 Old MCP: one waiter, one table number
0:21 MCP 2026-07-28: no handshake, no session ID
0:46 The takeaway

The takeaway: a server that remembers nothing is a server anyone can replace. If a server must remember something (a shopping basket), it hands back a ticket, an explicit handle, and the app passes it in again.

Try it: the TypeScript, Python, Go and C# MCP SDKs support 2026-07-28. Read the changelog first: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

Sources
MCP 2026-07-28 changelog: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog
SEP-2575, Make MCP Stateless: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2575-stateless-mcp
SEP-2567, Sessionless MCP via Explicit State Handles: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2567-sessionless-mcp
Release post by the MCP lead maintainers: https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/
Current version: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning
Before (2025-11-25): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle and https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports

The diner is an analogy: "table 12", "ticket #42" and the order on screen are invented examples.
Animation rendered from code. Voice by Kokoro, an open-source text-to-speech model.
